title: Return of the Shirt
cn: 第 4 集 · 那件旧衬衫
novel:
At the back of his [[wardrobe|wardrobe]], behind a [[dusty|dusty]] box, Ted found a [[faded|faded]] red shirt with a torn [[collar|collar]], a coffee [[stain|stain]] on one [[sleeve|sleeve]], and a small hole made by a [[moth|moth]].

He put it on. Suddenly he felt a wave of [[nostalgia|nostalgia]].

"Good shirts deserve a [[second chance|second chance]]," he announced. "And so do good girlfriends."

Lily warned him not to [[dig up|dig up]] the past. Ted was too [[sentimental|sentimental]] to listen. He opened a [[drawer|drawer]], found an old phone number, [[hesitated|hesitate]] for a second, and called his [[ex|ex]].

Her name was Natalie. She agreed to meet.

Dinner was strange and sweet. For twenty minutes the old [[spark|spark]] came back to life. Ted tried to [[revive|revive]] a joke from years ago; she laughed too late, and he [[cringed|cringe]].

Then he remembered why it had ended, and she remembered too. Some [[reunions|reunion]] are [[doomed|doomed]] before the first drink.

Walking home, Ted felt the memory [[fade|fade]] softly, like the colour of the shirt.

He kept the shirt anyway. Not everything old must be [[thrown away|throw away]] — but not everything old should be worn in public, either.

wardrobe.en: a tall cupboard where you keep your clothes

faded.en: with colour that has become weak and pale

collar.en: the part of a shirt that goes round your neck

stain.en: a dirty mark that is hard to wash off

sleeve.en: the part of clothing that covers your arm

moth.en: an insect like a butterfly that flies at night and eats cloth

nostalgia.en: a happy but slightly sad feeling about the past

second chance.en: another chance to do something better

dig up.en: to find old things or old facts that were hidden

sentimental.en: showing soft feelings about love or the past, sometimes too much

drawer.en: a box inside a desk that you pull out

hesitate.en: to stop for a moment because you are not sure

ex.en: a person you used to love, but not now

spark.en: a small bright feeling of excitement between two people

revive.en: to bring something back to life or back into use

cringe.en: to feel so ashamed that your body almost pulls back

reunion.en: a meeting of people who have not seen each other for a long time

doomed.en: certain to fail or end badly

fade.en: to slowly become weaker or less clear

throw away.en: to put something in the bin because you do not want it
